subject: Follow-up: Performance/SLO targets & benchmark methodology
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-24T16:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Performance targets and benchmark methodology

Hi Marissa — great conversation today, thanks for walking through Redwood's serving architecture. As discussed, wanted to capture our high-level performance/SLO targets and ask for your suggested benchmark methodology so we can validate before committing to Dedicated capacity.

Quick summary of our requirements:
- Latency: p95 target <= 200 ms; p99 <= 500 ms for interactive UI flows.
- Throughput: steady-state 500 QPS for batch inference endpoints (internal microservice consumers).
- Concurrency: up to 250 concurrent sessions for streaming chat with ~50 active streams at peak.
- Streaming: client-side streaming for progressive tokens is required; time-to-first-token (TTFT) ideally < 100 ms.
- Prompt characteristics: average prompt+response length ~120 tokens, 95th percentile of total sequence length ~600 tokens (occasionally up to 1024).

Can you share: prompt sets you plan to run, the eval harness (what we're measuring), and the definitions you use for warm vs cold runs, batching config, and KV cache behavior? Also curious how you measure token-level tail latencies for streaming.

I've attached our initial prompt set for reference (prompt_set_v2.csv). Happy to hop on another 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Head of ML Platform — EdgeFin
attachments: prompt_set_v2.csv (CSV)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T09:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets and benchmark methodology

Alex — thanks for the clear summary, and for sharing the prompt set. Super helpful. Below are the initial assumptions we'll use to design the benchmark; please review and flag anything that doesn't match EdgeFin's production behavior.

Planned benchmark methodology (high level):
- Two primary runs: latency-oriented (no batching, single-request paths, measure TTFT and per-token latency) and throughput-oriented (optimized batching, sustained QPS to measure throughput/efficiency).
- Warm vs cold: we'll define a warm state after 5k requests or 5 full-sequence cache fills (whichever comes first). Cold measurements will be taken on a fresh instance with no KV cache warmed.
- Streaming metrics: TTFT, per-token delta, 95/99/99.9 percentiles for both TTFT and per-token intervals. We'll capture both server-side and client-observed times when possible.
- Batching behavior: for latency runs we'll disable automatic batching and set max_batch_size=1. For throughput runs we'll tune batch sizes to match your sequence-length distribution. We'll also run a middle-ground "mixed" profile if you want to see trade-offs.
- Reproducibility: artifacts we will deliver — raw request logs, per-token timestamps, aggregated percentile tables, and the harness runnable via the attached template (redwood_benchmark_template.md).

Next steps I propose:
1) Confirm the prompt set and any additional edge-case prompts (long prompts, short prompts, mult-turn).
2) Share target model version (or family) and whether quantized variants are acceptable for initial runs.
3) Give us a window for a benchmark run (we have capacity next week).

I'll loop in David for measurement definitions and Dev for harness ownership.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_benchmark_template.md (stub)
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-02-25T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets and benchmark methodology

Internal notes / measurement suggestions:
- Streaming: measure TTFT (time from request start to first token) and then token-delta distribution (time between consecutive tokens). For p99.9 we should use at least 100k token observations to avoid statistical noise.
- Warmup: 10k to 50k requests depending on sequence length. For reproducibility, we should script deterministic seeds and a fixed replay order for prompts.
- Environment: capture GPU model, CUDA/cuDNN/ROCm versions, kernel, and instance sizing. Also snapshot model config (sequence length caps, kv-cache settings, quantization).
- Metrics: p50/p90/p95/p99/p99.9 and 99.99 (if sample size allows) for TTFT and per-token latency; aggregate tokens/sec and token-cost.
- Duration: for throughput testing, run at target QPS for a minimum of 30 minutes to capture autoscaling behavior; for latency runs, run bursts of 10k requests with pauses for garbage collection profiling.

Dev — can you prep the harness (container + runbook) and make sure logs include per-token timestamps and request IDs so we can correlate client/server views?

Thanks,
David
Director, Performance Engineering — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Benchmark Labs <bench@labs.com>
Date: 2026-02-26T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets and benchmark methodology

Marissa, David — thanks for the thoughtful plan. A few clarifications from our side:
- Model family: we'll start with finetuned-Redwood-7B (production variant). Quantized 4-bit variants are acceptable for the throughput-oriented run but we'd like a non-quantized baseline for latency-sensitive flows.
- Prompt distribution: average 120 tokens; attached prompt_set_v2.csv includes ~2k samples. We'll add 150 long-tail (>=800 tokens) prompts in a follow-up message.
- Streaming: client expects server-sent events style streaming; TTFT is critical for UX.
- Environment: most production traffic comes from US-east with clients on modern browsers; requests are TLS, authenticated with signed JWTs.

We uploaded our internal SLO spreadsheet (slo_targets.xlsx) — includes the business impact mapping to p95/p99 targets. HubSpot deal link: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/EDG-4123

We can provide access to a staging project (service account) so Redwood can run the harness against a representative endpoint next week.

Regards,
Alex Turner
Head of ML Platform — EdgeFin
attachments: prompt_set_v2.csv, slo_targets.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@edgefin.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T08:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Performance targets and benchmark methodology

Alex — this all looks good. We outlined an executable plan below and attached the harness we typically use for partner benchmarks.

Execution plan (what Redwood will run):
- Latency run (interactive profile): disable batching, concurrent streams = 32, run bursts of 10k requests to warm and then capture cold vs warm percentiles (TTFT & per-token).
- Throughput run (efficiency profile): enable batching, target sustained 500 QPS for 30 minutes, measure tokens/sec, cost-per-token, and p95/p99 tail behavior.
- Mixed profile: one run with moderate batching and concurrency to show trade-offs.

Deliverables: raw per-request/per-token logs, aggregated percentile tables (CSV), a reproducible runbook, and an artifacts folder in the shared Drive link. We'll also include a short readme with the exact config (model pins, batch sizes, warmup counts).

Attachments included: benchmark_harness_v1.zip (containerized harness), slo_table.xlsx (example of aggregated outputs).

Schedule: we can run the benchmarks the week of Mar 8. Proposal: run latency-oriented tests on Mon Mar 8 AM PST and throughput tests Tue Mar 9 AM PST; sync to review results Wed Mar 10 at 10:00 AM PT — does that work for you?

Access: please create a staging service account with write access to the Drive folder and share SSH/endpoint details.

Next steps for EdgeFin: share long-tail prompts (>=800 tokens), confirm the model variant to pin for the baseline, and create the staging service account.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
